West Germany, the Federal Republic of Germany, was the democratic German state formed in 1949 from the British, American and French occupation zones. Its capital was the small university town of Bonn. It lasted, under that name, until reunification in 1990.

Its constitution, the Basic Law, was built to avoid the failures of the Weimar years. Its first chancellor, Konrad Adenauer, tied it firmly to the West: it joined NATO in 1955 and was a founding member of the European Economic Community under the Treaty of Rome in 1957.

The 1950s brought the economic miracle, helped by the Marshall Plan, a stable currency and millions of skilled refugees. Labour shortages brought guest workers, many of them from Turkey. Later Willy Brandt reached out to the East. In 1990 East Germany joined the Federal Republic, and the reunited country kept its name and constitution.
